title: Drawing ROIs in ITK-Snap
author: Courtney Comrie
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8nvhve6
materials: Change the Presegmentation mode to Classification from Thresholding.

steps.title: Launch ITK‑SNAP via Singularity
steps.instruction: Open a terminal and run: cd /rsgrps/hutchinsone/Singularity_Containers; module load singularity; singularity run nklab-neurotools-v0.4.sif itksnap

steps.title: Load NIFTI image
steps.instruction: In ITK‑SNAP, open the desired NIFTI file.

steps.title: Zoom to desired view
steps.instruction: Select the “Zoom/Pan Mode” button, then click the up‑arrow to zoom until the brain region of interest is clearly visible.

steps.title: Identify target ROI
steps.instruction: Consult the Ferret Brain Atlas (or other resources) to locate the tract you wish to segment.

steps.title: Draw ROI manually
steps.instruction: Select “Polygon Mode”, trace the outline of the ROI on the current slice, then click the Accept button in the bottom‑right corner.

steps.title: Continue manual tracing
steps.instruction: Repeat the polygon tracing on successive slices until the ROI is fully delineated.

steps.title: Save manual ROI
steps.instruction: Choose Segmentation → Save Segmentation Image, give the file a name, and delete the “.gz” extension so the file is saved as “.nii”.

steps.title: Verify saved ROI
steps.instruction: Re‑open the saved .nii file in ITK‑SNAP to confirm the segmentation is correct.

steps.title: Launch ITK‑SNAP for snake tool
steps.instruction: Repeat the launch command (cd …; module load singularity; singularity run … itksnap) to start a new session.

steps.title: Load NIFTI image again
steps.instruction: Open the same NIFTI file in the new ITK‑SNAP session.

steps.title: Activate snake segmentation
steps.instruction: Select the snake tool in the top‑left corner, then click the “Segment 3D” button.

steps.title: Zoom for snake tool
steps.instruction: Again, use Zoom/Pan Mode and the up‑arrow to obtain a comfortable view of the brain.

steps.title: Create training labels
steps.instruction: Train the classifier by marking the ROI and surrounding tissue with multiple labels.

substeps.instruction: Mark the ROI with Label 1 using polygon or paintbrush mode
Create additional label(s) to mark areas that are not the ROI
Add 2–4 more labels (total 3–5) and retrain until the ROI is isolated from surrounding grey and white matter

steps.title: Clear training marks (optional)
steps.instruction: If you need to restart, select “Clear Examples” to delete all polygon/brush marks.

steps.title: Proceed to segmentation
steps.instruction: When satisfied with the classifier, click “Next” in the bottom‑right corner.

steps.title: Place initial bubble
steps.instruction: Move the cursor over the ROI and click “Add Bubble at Cursor”; adjust bubble size and placement, then click “Next”.

steps.title: Grow bubble to final ROI
steps.instruction: Press the play button to grow the bubble; optionally click “Update” (bottom‑left) to view the 3‑D visualization of the evolving ROI.

steps.title: Save snake‑derived ROI
steps.instruction: Choose Segmentation → Save Segmentation Image, name the file, and remove the “.gz” extension so it is saved as a “.nii” file.
